title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A boundary the keystroke path could not see
summary: Last release taught the forced unwrap highlight to see comment blocks. It did not teach the keystroke path to notice when one opens or closes, so the highlight only followed the comment after an unrelated event rebuilt the file.

highlights.title: The highlight follows the comment
highlights.description: Typing the start of a comment above a highlighted unwrap left the highlight standing on code that had just become documentation.

highlights.title: Deleting a boundary counts too
highlights.description: A change event carries what was typed, never what was removed. Each line now remembers whether it held a boundary, so losing one triggers the rebuild.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The full rebuild already fired when a raw string boundary moved. It now fires for comment boundaries as well.
Ordinary typing still takes the incremental path, one line at a time.
